skills.name: find-skills
skills.summary: Discover and install specialized agent skills from the open ecosystem when users need extended capabilities.
skills.solves: 让 agent 自己发现并安装 skill，是全站入口级元技能
quotes: Provides `npx skills find [query]` command to search interactively and `npx skills add <package>` to install from GitHub or other sources
Recommends skills based on install count (prefer 1K+), source reputation (official sources like Vercel, Anthropic), and GitHub stars to ensure quality
Checks the skills.sh leaderboard first for battle-tested, popular options before running CLI searches

skills.name: grill-me
skills.summary: Relentless interviewing skill that stress-tests plans and designs through systematic questioning.
skills.solves: AI 编程最高频失败模式「它做的不是你要的」——开工前把需求问透
quotes: Conducts deep-dive questioning across all aspects of a plan, walking through decision trees branch-by-branch until shared understanding is reached
Automatically explores the codebase to answer questions where code context is available, reducing redundant back-and-forth
Designed for design reviews, architecture validation, and pre-implementation planning where thorough vetting prevents downstream issues

skills.name: tdd
skills.summary: Test-driven development with vertical slices, behavior-focused tests, and incremental red-green-refactor cycles.
skills.solves: AI 写的测试测实现细节、一重构就全红——强制测行为、在接缝上测
quotes: Emphasizes integration-style tests that verify behavior through public APIs, not implementation details; tests should survive refactors unchanged
Requires vertical slicing (one test → one implementation → repeat) instead of horizontal slicing (all tests first, then all code)
A seam is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.
Test only at pre-agreed seams. Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user.

skills.name: improve-codebase-architecture
skills.summary: Analyze codebases for architectural friction and propose module-deepening refactors as testability improvements.
skills.solves: agent 加速编码也加速软件熵增——定期体检代码库，找出该加深的模块
quotes: Explores codebases organically to surface shallow modules, tightly-coupled components, and untested seams rather than following rigid heuristics
Applies John Ousterhout's "deep module" principle: small interfaces hiding large implementations for better testability and AI navigability
Generates multiple radically different interface designs (minimalist, flexible, caller-optimized, ports & adapters) via parallel sub-agents, then recommends the strongest approach
It is a survey, not a rescue: on a genuinely old codebase it will find real candidates, but it won't untangle the mud for you.

skills.name: handoff
skills.summary: Summarize conversations into handoff documents for seamless agent-to-agent transitions.
skills.solves: 上下文满了/换 agent/中断时，无损压缩上下文而不是从头讲一遍
quotes: Compacts current conversation context into a structured document saved to the OS temp directory
Automatically suggests relevant skills the next agent should invoke based on conversation content
Avoids duplication by referencing existing artifacts (PRDs, plans, ADRs, issues, commits, diffs) by path or URL rather than repeating their content
Redacts sensitive data including API keys, passwords, and personally identifiable information before handoff

Write a handoff document summarising the current conversation so a fresh agent can continue the work. Save to the temporary directory of the user's OS ($TMPDIR, else /tmp; %TEMP% on Windows) - not the current workspace.

skills.name: triage
skills.summary: State machine-driven issue triage with role-based workflow management and agent brief generation.
skills.solves: issue 堆积状态混乱；且主动标注 AI 生成避免误导
skills.warning: 安全审计 Warn —— 装前须自行审 SKILL.md（它会自动往 issue tracker 发评论）
quotes: Two category roles (bug, enhancement) and five state roles (needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix)
Includes reproduction testing for bugs, grilling sessions for incomplete issues, and templates for triage notes and agent briefs
Every comment or issue posted to the issue tracker during triage must start with this disclaimer: > *This was generated by AI during triage.*

skills.name: frontend-design
skills.summary: Distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces that reject generic AI aesthetics through intentional design choices.
skills.solves: AI 生成的界面千篇一律——强制先定美学方向再写代码
quotes: Guides aesthetic direction selection (brutalist, maximalist, retro-futuristic, luxury, organic, etc.) before implementation
Explicitly avoids overused fonts, clichéd color schemes, and predictable layouts that characterize generic AI-generated interfaces
Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's.
a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option

skills.name: research
skills.summary: Spin up a background agent to do the research, so you keep working while it reads.
skills.solves: 研究不阻塞干活，且每条结论都要溯源到一手资料
quotes: Investigate the question against primary sources (official docs, source code, specs, first-party APIs), not a secondary write-up of them. Follow every claim back to the source that owns it.
Write the findings to a single Markdown file, citing each claim's source.
Save it where the repo already keeps such notes

skills.name: design-mobile-apps
skills.summary: Designing with Sleek — 通过 sleek.design REST API 创建项目、从 brief 设计屏幕、取回 HTML 与渲染图
skills.warning: Snyk: Fail。且 GitHub 仅 15 star 却有 80 万安装（比值 5.3 万倍）—— 商业推广驱动，非社区认可
quotes: sleek.design provides a REST API at /api/v1/* to create projects, design screens from a brief, and fetch their HTML and renders.
Auth: Authorization: Bearer $SLEEK_API_KEY

skills.name: reddit-automation
skills.summary: 在 Reddit 找真正需要你产品的人，诚实披露身份后回复
skills.solves: Reddit 营销：真实贡献而非刷屏
quotes: Reddit rewards real contribution and punishes spam. The way to market here is not to hide — it's to genuinely help, disclose your affiliation, and only bring up your product when it truly answers the question.
This skill runs two moves: find the few threads where you can actually help, then draft a reply worth posting.
